bounded-context.name: Lexicon loading
bounded-context.purpose: Read a lexicon-conform project's XML files from disk, validate them against schema v1.0 with a typed traversal, resolve typed cross-references between entities, and produce a `ResolvedGraph` the client can render. Surfaces load issues (parse errors, schema errors, version mismatches, dangling refs) without failing the whole load.
bounded-context.narrative:
The loader runs in three passes. First it walks `lexicon/`, reads every XML file, parses with `xast-util-from-xml`, and dispatches on the root element name (`<system>`, `<bounded-context>`, `<surface>`) into a typed traversal that builds a `LexiconFile` shape. Any single-file failure becomes a ; the loader never throws (). Then it registers every entity as a keyed by — duplicates raise an error issue and the second registration is dropped ().
The second pass is : structural `<ref to="..."/>` elements in XML (a term's `<disambiguates-from>`, an aggregate's `<members>`, a seam's `<upstream>`/`<downstream>`, omission `<related-atoms>`) are looked up against the registered map with owner-scoped fallbacks first (including kernel-owner scope for kernel-owned atoms), then common shorthands. Unresolved refs become warnings (). The third pass scans every prose-bearing field for inline `<ref/>` elements (collapsed to `[[fqid]]` markers during parse) and runs the same resolver — a dangling prose ref is the same severity as a dangling structural ref.
An short-circuits the whole pipeline on unchanged files; `?refresh=1` clears every project's cache () so the user's "Refresh" button is a strong signal that means *re-read from disk*. The viewer is a triage surface as much as a reader — every issue rides along on `ResolvedGraph.issues` so the user can fix their XML in-place rather than chase parse errors.

term.name: ResolvedGraph
term.definition: The post-load representation delivered to the client. Holds `system` (the system root entity), `entities` (a flat map of fqid → ResolvedEntity), `byKind` (fqids grouped by entity kind), `issues` (LoadIssues collected during parse + resolve), and `projectRoot`. The full structure ships over the wire on every `GET /api/projects/:id/lexicon`.

term.name: ResolvedEntity
term.definition: One node of the `ResolvedGraph`. Carries a typed `ref: EntityRef`, the `ownerContextId` (null for system-level / surfaces / shared kernels), an optional `ownerKernelId` for kernel-owned atoms, the `source.file` for git history and audit purposes, an optional `xastNode` reference for future editor-mode AST↔model navigation, and entity-kind-specific typed fields (definition, statement, rationale, body, anchors, category, seam kind, aggregate root, …). Every cold-layer entity — system, bounded-context, term, invariant, seam, boundary-rule, aggregate, module, shared-kernel, surface, region — becomes one ResolvedEntity.

term.name: EntityRef
term.definition: The smallest pointer to an entity: `{kind, fqid, name}`. Used everywhere the graph references another entity (disambiguatesFrom, contains, regions, aggregate root/members/invariants, seam upstream/downstream, service operatesOn, event consumers). Cheap to embed in many places without duplicating prose.

term.name: LoadIssue
term.definition: A single parse / schema / resolution failure: `{file, message, severity}` with severity `error` (file couldn't be loaded) or `warning` (loaded but something inside is wrong — typically a dangling ref). Issues ride along with `ResolvedGraph.issues`; the loader never throws on a bad file.

term.name: ref resolution
term.definition: The second pass of the loader, where structural `<ref to="..."/>` elements in XML (e.g. a term's `<disambiguates-from><ref to="other-term"/>`) are looked up against the registered entity map. The resolver tries owner-scoped lookups first (sibling in the same context, or sibling in the same shared kernel), then qualified forms (`<ctx>/<slug>`, `kernel/<kid>/<slug>`), then common shorthands (`context/<slug>`, `kernel/<slug>`, `surface/<slug>`). Unresolved refs become warnings — they don't block the load.
term.returns: A resolved `EntityRef` if the slug matched, or null (with a warning `LoadIssue` appended to the project's issue list).

term.name: mtime cache
term.definition: The loader keeps a per-`projectRoot` cache keyed by the latest mtime across all XML files in the project's `lexicon/` dir. A subsequent load with the same latest-mtime returns the cached `ResolvedGraph` without re-parsing. The cache is invalidated explicitly on `refresh=1` query and on project removal.

invariant.name: fqid uniqueness within a graph
invariant.statement: Every entity registered in a `ResolvedGraph` has a globally unique `fqid`. Duplicates surface as an error `LoadIssue` and the second registration is dropped.
invariant.rationale: `fqid`s are used as React keys, route params, and graph node IDs. Duplicates would silently break navigation and rendering. Surfacing as a load-time error lets the user fix the XML before debugging UI glitches.

invariant.name: bad XML produces issues, not exceptions
invariant.statement: Any single-file failure (read error, XML parse error, schema mismatch, dangling ref) is recorded as a `LoadIssue` and the loader continues with the remaining files. The graph response is always well-formed JSON.
invariant.rationale: The viewer is a triage surface as much as a reader — it should help the user *see* problems in their cold layer, not refuse to render when one file is broken. Forward progress beats fail-fast in a read-only tool.

invariant.name: refresh=1 invalidates the cache globally
invariant.statement: `GET /api/projects/:id/lexicon?refresh=1` calls `invalidateCache()` with no argument, clearing every project's cached graph. Subsequent loads re-read from disk.
invariant.rationale: The viewer is a single-user dev tool; the user clicking "Refresh" is the strong signal that they want fresh data. Clearing all caches keeps the logic simple and avoids "stale despite refresh" surprises if the file mtime hasn't changed (e.g., a `touch -m` of the same content).

invariant.name: dangling refs are warnings, not errors
invariant.statement: An unresolved ref (e.g., a term's `<disambiguates-from>` pointing at a slug no entity claims) produces a `severity: warning` LoadIssue, not an error. The owning entity loads with that ref simply absent from its resolved field.
invariant.rationale: Real lexicon authoring often involves renames mid-flight; a dangling ref is a signal to fix in `lex-crystallize`, not a load failure. Same forward-progress principle as `loader-never-throws`.
